title: Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) Levy Collection Bill 2018
short_title: Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) Levy Collection Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish collection arrangements for a domestic commercial vessel levy administered by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA), including deadlines and late payment penalties.
The annual levy would be due at the end of 28 July, while a proportional levy would be payable 28 days after a vessel became liable.

Its main provisions would commence with the companion levy legislation, alongside separate consequential amendments supporting enforcement and payment arrangements under existing maritime safety laws.
changes: The Minister could allow quarterly instalments through rules instead of requiring a single annual payment.
Late payment penalties could be set by rules up to 20 per cent annually on unpaid amounts, with remission and review safeguards.
AMSA would have to refund excess levy payments, instalments and late payment penalties.
Levy liabilities and late payment penalties would be Commonwealth debts recoverable through the courts.
summary.affected: People liable for the domestic commercial vessel levy and AMSA would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Damian Drum
speeches.brief: The Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) Levy Collection Bill 2018 defines when the levy on domestic commercial vessels is due and payable, allows payment by instalment, imposes a late payment penalty, permits advance payment, requires refunds of overpayments, and empowers the minister to make rules for the act.
